Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: opaque pixel-style RPG battle environment for an existing hack-and-slash game.
Input roles: Image 1 is the environment edit target. Image 2 is the hunter sprite style reference only. Image 3 is the chitin creature sprite style reference only. Do not place characters, creatures or sprite sheets in the output.
Primary request: Repaint the environment from image 1 so it convincingly belongs to the SAME game as the hunter and creature. Keep the giant beast carapace battlefield concept, slate armor plates, ivory bone ridges, sparse teal growth and thin amber fissures. Rebuild the rendering style; do not merely color-grade the old detailed floor.
Style: hand-crafted 16-bit-inspired pixel game art with strong clean stepped silhouettes, visible consistent square pixel clusters, deliberately simplified shapes and 3-4 flat shade bands per material. Match the sprites' warm ivory highlights, slate-grey armor, dark desaturated brown outlines and muted teal accents. Broad readable polygonal armor plates with short, sparse chips. No dense stipple, grain, photographic rock texture, painterly gradients, or realistic rendering.
Scene: a broad open playable field seen from an elevated three-quarter game camera, no horizon. The center 80 percent is traversable slate carapace with medium-size plate boundaries, gentle changes of shade and sparse chips for navigation, not a blank rectangle. Keep ivory bone ridges and taller growth near the outer perimeter, with only small low details inside. Ground shadows and visible front faces must match the sprites' camera.
Lighting: one soft warm light from upper left, modest contrast, warm neutral shadows, no independent blue ambient wash. Background contrast less than the character sprites so they remain readable without looking pasted on.
Composition: wide landscape map texture, a single coherent environment, consistent scale throughout, no artificial depth blur or vignette. No UI, text, frame, grid, cutaway, people, monster bodies, weapons, loot, attack effects or watermark. Entire opaque image filled with the environment.
